title: Zoom in: one minute window from first click to final row
caption: A window opens on its first event, closes when the watermark passes its end plus the allowed lateness, and only then writes its row.

messages.label: open window (ad7, 09:14)
messages.note: The bucket is ts // 60: the window is found from the event time, not the arrival time.

messages.label: more clicks for 09:14
messages.note: In-memory count and spend; nothing is written yet.

messages.label: watermark passes 09:15 + 10 s
messages.note: The watermark says 'no event older than this is expected any more'.

messages.label: ack
messages.note: Only now is the window's state dropped and the checkpoint advanced.

scenarios.name: Late click, still allowed
scenarios.summary: A phone was offline for a few seconds. Its click lands inside the allowed lateness and updates the open window.

messages.label: add to (ad7, 09:14)
messages.note: The watermark has not passed 09:15 + 10 s yet, so the window is still open.

scenarios.name: Straggler after close
scenarios.summary: A click shows up an hour late. Reopening windows forever would keep unbounded state; route it aside and let the nightly recon count it.

messages.label: click ad7 @ 09:14:30, arrives 10:20
messages.note: Buffered on a device that was offline.

messages.label: side output: count as late
messages.note: A late-events metric; the raw archive still has the event.

messages.label: no change tonight; recon will include it
messages.note: The streaming row stays slightly low until the batch recompute overwrites it.

scenarios.name: Write ack lost
scenarios.summary: The upsert succeeds but its ack is lost. The retry writes the same absolute value, so the row is still right.

messages.label: ack
messages.note: Network blip: the write happened, the reply did not arrive.

messages.label: retry: upsert (ad7, 09:14) = 42 clicks
messages.note: Setting 42 twice is still 42. An 'add 42' write would now say 84.
